claims.quote: This year's report found that 46 per cent of students in OECD countries use AI, like ChatGPT or Claude, weekly to help them learn, and it's slightly higher in Australia at the rate of 50 per cent.

claims.source_notes: Release on 8 Sep 2026 per news coverage (TechNode, 8 Sep 2026); OECD page returned 403. Australia 50% (vs OECD 45.5%) confirmed by ACS Information Age, 9 Sep 2026 (https://ia.acs.org.au/article/2026/govt-blames-technology-as-student-scores-hit-record-low.html).
claims.vintage_rationale: Latest PISA figures, released the day before the debate.

claims.quote: It also found that smartphones and AI chatbots were accelerating a global educational decline that is robbing students of the ability to concentrate, interpret and reason.
claims.supporting_quote: Overnight, the Programme for International Student Assessment 2025 report was released from the OECD in Paris.
claims.claim: PISA 2025 found that smartphones and AI chatbots are accelerating a global decline in educational performance.

claims.vintage_rationale: OECD presents AI-use findings as associations and lists several possible causes of decline; a causal 'accelerating' claim overstates the report.
